title: Why the TTP Remains the Central Fault Line Between Pakistan and Afghanistan
gist: Cross-border clashes in October, including Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan and an attempted crossing in Kurram, show the TTP as the central fault line between Pakistan and Afghanistan's Taliban government.

insights.claim: On October 11 Pakistan's military said it killed 12 militants and Afghan Taliban personnel during an attempted crossing into Kurram district, with Afghan Taliban border posts firing in support and one Pakistani soldier killed.
insights.speaker: Natasha Matloob
insights.so_what: Direct Taliban-army exchanges signal rising risk of broader border conflict.

insights.claim: Ten days earlier Pakistani airstrikes in Afghanistan reportedly killed 22 militants, while UNAMA confirmed at least 10 civilians, mostly children, killed in Kunar and Helmand.
insights.speaker: Natasha Matloob
insights.so_what: Civilian casualties invite UN and regional pressure and could fuel retaliation.
